caption:
🇬🇧 UK Daily Briefing | Thursday, 29 October 2026

1. 💷 Healey unveils £100 towards energy bills and bank tax in first Budget
Chancellor Healey announced £100 towards energy bills and a tax on banks in his first Budget, aimed at easing the cost of living. Opposition parties say he has not been bold enough.

2. 🚭 Scotland bans sale of nicotine products to under-18s
The ban forms part of the Tobacco and Vapes Act 2026.

3. 🎓 Government to allow two-year graduate visa for 'high-compliance' universities
The government will also expand the 'high potential individual' visa route to the top 150 global institutions, as part of efforts to attract 'the world's best graduates'.

4. ⚖️ New respect orders come into force to target antisocial behaviour
Perpetrators of antisocial behaviour could face tougher restrictions as new respect orders come into force across England and Wales today.

5. ✈️ More than 4m illegal cigarettes seized at Manchester Airport
Border Force officers seized more than 4 million illegal cigarettes, worth an estimated £2.59 million, during a four-day crackdown at Manchester Airport.

6. 💰 Households in Wales will receive £100 energy payment, minister confirms
Wales's finance minister has confirmed the £100 payment to help with bills. The Chancellor announced it in Wednesday's Budget, telling MPs the devolved nations would receive "their share" of funding.

7. ⚽ Russo hat-trick makes her England's top Women's Champions League scorer
Alessia Russo scored a hat-trick in Arsenal's 3-0 win over Benfica, becoming England's all-time leading goalscorer in the Women's Champions League.

8. 👑 King Charles shows off dance moves on second day of Caribbean tour
Earlier in the day, the King paid his respects to the island's fallen servicemen and women.

Sources: BBC, The Independent, GOV.UK Home Office, Nation.Cymru, BBC Sport. Stories summarised from UK media reports. Images: Pixabay.
